column5: Ultrasonic moduli are not audio-band. Laemmlein's audio-band plates give G_LR 1580 MPa against Sonderegger's ultrasonic 1680, and E_L 12500 / E_R 1550 MPa against Sonderegger's static 10900 / 1175 (inplane=laemmlein). Neither source is the il Cannone's wood. A violin-grade (curly, resonance) maple of the committed Spycher pack has E_L about 9700 to 10000 MPa and E_R about 1650 to 1700 MPa dynamically. Axis convention: material axis 1 = L (grain), axis 2 = R (across the growth rings, in the plane of a quartersawn plate), thickness = T, so shear_modulus_12 = G_LR, shear_modulus_13 = G_LT and shear_modulus_23 = G_RT, poisson_ratio_12 = nu_LR (strain along R per strain along L under stress along L; the source's subscripts were converted to this order in the committed Sonderegger pack). The validity band omega 2 pi 150 to 2 pi 10000 rad/s is the narrower of the sources' bands: Laemmlein's loss factors and audio-band G_LR come from a loudspeaker sweep over 150-10000 Hz (four plate modes of it, whose frequencies the source does not state), and the static and 1 MHz ultrasonic moduli bracket the audio band. Using a static or ultrasonic modulus inside the band is a STATED ASSUMPTION that the audio-band value lies between the two, with no dispersion applied; it is not a fit. T 280 to 320 K is the band in which this use is DECLARED by the pack author, not a measured band.
